one_star_reviews.text:
I recommend looking for other dentists. I went for a checkup because I couldn't go to my usual dentist, who had good reviews. As a result, they told me I needed root canals in several teeth and fillings in a few others. Given the urgency they presented, I started the treatments. Luckily, I only started with one filling, which I knew I needed. When I consulted another dentist I trust, the diagnosis was two fillings, but he said I didn't need any root canals because the situation wasn't nearly as serious, and I certainly didn't have that many cavities.

I'm no longer worried about them trying to rip me off, since a complaint would be enough to get it back. The problem is that they would have done a terrible job on my teeth unnecessarily.

If anyone is thinking of going here, seek advice elsewhere because you probably don't need half of what they tell you here. I'm very sorry for anyone who fell for this scam.

one_star_reviews.text:
The experience was quite unpleasant. It's a very aggressive sales tactic, and I feel like I've been scammed like never before, especially considering the underhanded way they handled the whole process. So, think things through very carefully before they trap you like they did me.

It all started with the "consultation"—three of us went to see the doctor about a "SPECIAL OFFER" on hyaluronic acid… and what a surprise! The offer was for "one vial," and you need another one for the other half of your face! 🤣 Yes, really! The offer is only for half your face. The "fine print" is that it's only for half the offer; the other half doesn't fit in the door. So, the price jumps from €200 to €400. Imagine the dumbfounded look on my face! I mean, €200 MORE for another vial because I need two, and this guy conveniently forgot to mention that two vials are needed for a full face treatment. In what world is an offer for half a face?! And of course, the Botox they were "offering" "isn't as strong for men," and naturally, what does that mean? Another €60 more.

Of course, he tells you this after you've signed all the paperwork and you're there to see who goes first... three people in the tiny room, under pressure to get it done right away, no time to react, no time to think—a classic setup. And when you leave there you're like, "But... what have I done?!" The whole thing ended up costing me almost €300 more. (€300 more for two people and €60 more for the third, €660 more because there was missing information in the offer)

And the kicker is that there's no "touch-up" after 15 days, it's a "revision," and what was the next "surprise"?! Two of us had to get a "touch-up" because we insisted, since their strategy was that none of the three of us needed any touch-up... and the final straw is that they used only ONE remaining vial (there were 3 of us and they used only 1 vial for the touch-up) and they touched up TWO of us!

I repeat! A single vial of touch-up was used for two people, and the doctor insisted to the third that they didn't need any touch-up, even when that person mentioned a slight difference in height between the two sides of their face.

I was astonished the first time I went; I couldn't react to the underhanded and aggressive sales tactics. But after the touch-up, I couldn't believe he could be so unprofessional, using such methods to deceive people, and using only one vial of touch-up for everyone.

I was shocked when I went. And yes, I made sure to check how many vials for touch-ups were on the table where he keeps the materials, and to see that there was ONLY ONE VIAL FOR TWO PEOPLE, I couldn't believe what I was seeing, and what I was doing...

So please, DON'T TRUST HIM, ask everything before doing anything, because this man is trying to squeeze money out of you at every turn. It's not normal to go in for €400 and leave having paid almost €700. ALMOST DOUBLE!

A COMPLETE DISAPPOINTMENT
I've had an electric vehicle for almost a year now, and it's been giving me problems practically from the start, especially with energy consumption, range, and charging.

I've taken the vehicle to the official service center several times, even leaving it there for up to two weeks. The response I've repeatedly received is that "the car is fine," but every time I start using it normally again, the problems reappear.
I followed their instructions for using the vehicle normally, even driving at normal speeds and using the air conditioning without trying to conserve battery power. For a few days, it seemed to improve, but then it went back to consuming an excessive amount of battery and charging slowly, even stopping altogether.

I have photos of different journeys and charging issues. I've experienced battery drain of around 50% to get to Elda and over 30% to return, and on very short trips, I've recorded drains of 12%, 13%, 14%, 15%, and even 16%.

The worst part is that this isn't just an inconvenience: it's causing me significant financial and personal problems. I have to frequently use public charging stations, sometimes costing €16, €20, or even €32, and other times I have to wait for hours to charge the vehicle.

I've even had situations where I haven't been able to use the car for important appointments because the battery wasn't sufficient or the charging was interrupted.
When I bought the vehicle, I was told it would have a range of about 320 km and that an electric car would save me money. The reality has been very different: at 100% charge, it reached approximately 281 km, and currently it's around 274 km.
After almost a year, I'm still in the exact same situation. I don't want another service appointment just to be told again that the car is fine. I want a permanent solution.

The service I've received so far has left me deeply disappointed. I expected that, after so many visits to the official service center and repeatedly explaining the same problem, someone would finally take responsibility and find a real solution. A vehicle that I need for my daily life cannot be parked outside my house and not allow me to rely on it.

I went to Isla Pool Club and, overall, I think it's a place with a lot of potential. The location is fantastic, the space is very well maintained, and the staff is friendly and attentive. There's also a pretty decent selection of food and drinks, so in many ways, it has all the ingredients to be an excellent place.

However, I think they're really hurting themselves with their music choices. The volume is too high, and frankly, the music is quite bad and very intrusive, to the point of ruining the atmosphere. Furthermore, it seems to encourage rather uncouth behavior and attitudes that don't fit with the ambiance the place could have.

I asked about it, and they told me they use the same type of music throughout the season. I think they have a very simple opportunity here to significantly improve the experience. With a little more effort and variety in their music selection—and by adapting it to the time of day and the atmosphere—they could attract many more people and probably generate a lot more business at the bar.

It's a shame, because everything else is quite good: a great location, well-maintained facilities, friendly staff, and a reasonable selection of food and drinks. Changing and diversifying the music seems like a relatively simple solution that could make a huge difference. They really should consider it, because as it is now, they're shooting themselves in the foot.

one_star_reviews.text: Don't buy cars here! I bought a Seat Ibiza from him for €6,000, and when I got it from Bilbao to Madrid, the tires were bald, the headlights were stuck together, and it was leaking oil from the gasket and the oil pan cover. The worst part is that I made him change the tires right then and there, and he didn't even balance them. I had to pay in Madrid before I even left so I could get back safely. I'm writing this review again so people can see what a scammer he is. I had to drive him crazy with calls to get him to pay for the car's maintenance, which I hadn't even had for two days. He kept saying he'd done all the maintenance, and when we changed the oil, it was blacker than the money he pays his employees, who aren't even on the books! Think carefully about where you spend your money because this guy is going to rip you off one way or another. Right in front of me, I saw a mechanic call him over and tell him to manually adjust the temperature gauge on a Ford, because the customer who was going to buy the car wanted the needle to go up to 90, as the customer said it wasn't reaching 90. The mechanic told his own mechanic to raise it by hand because the customer wasn't satisfied. That says it all. He tricked me, but with my contribution, we can help shut down businesses like this.

It pains me to leave a negative review, but after my experience, I feel it's necessary to share it.

I bought my car here in February 2024 with approximately 133,000 km on the odometer. At the time of purchase, it appeared to be in very good condition. However, since then, I've had to deal with numerous problems and expenses.

About a month after buying it, the xenon headlights burned out.

Nine months after purchase, I had to replace all four tires because they had very little tread remaining. I understand that tires are wear items and that this isn't necessarily the seller's responsibility, but I feel it's important to mention it in my experience with the vehicle, especially given how recently I bought it.

A year and five months after purchase, the water pump broke, causing problems with the coolant.

About two and a half years after purchase, the left engine mount was practically broken and had to be replaced.

Unfortunately, the most serious problem came later. The car started experiencing a significant loss of power, vibrations, and other performance issues, so I had to take it to a garage. After inspection, a serious problem was diagnosed in cylinder number 2 of the engine, with oil present/accumulating in that cylinder.

According to the garage's diagnosis, the repair requires replacing the entire engine block, as individual cylinder replacement is not an option for this engine. This repair alone costs over €3,000, and additional costs may arise once the engine is disassembled.

I bought the vehicle with approximately 133,000 km on the odometer, and it currently has around 163,000 km. In other words, in just 30,000 km since I bought it, I've had to deal with all these problems, culminating in a serious engine failure whose cost is forcing me to consider selling the car.

I understand that I bought a used vehicle and that a used car can experience breakdowns and require replacement of worn parts. However, due to the number of problems that have arisen, and especially because it ended with an engine failure of this magnitude after only 30,000 km since purchase, my experience has been very disappointing.

I expected to be able to enjoy the car for many more kilometers before finding myself in a situation like this.

one_star_reviews.text:
I first contacted this center on March 3, 2026, because I was very interested in their one-on-one personal training sessions, especially because of the technology, the support, and the positive reviews.

From the beginning, I explained my situation and that I didn't yet speak Spanish. I also explained that I would soon be starting Spanish lessons at home. If language was going to be a problem, I would have preferred that they tell me clearly. I would have understood perfectly.

I live in Estepona with my parents, and we are trying to start a new life here. I've had a difficult life; I have a disability, and I was specifically looking for personalized support to help me regain confidence and move forward. That's why this concept particularly interested me.

After several months without receiving a response to my WhatsApp messages, my mother went to the center in person this week. She explained the situation, left my Spanish phone number and email address, and the trainer told her he would send me the prices and information.

I received nothing.

On Tuesday, I also sent one last private message via Instagram. It appeared as read on Wednesday. Today is Friday and I still haven't received any response, not even a simple message telling me to wait.

I have screenshots of my messages and everything that's happened.

I'm not asking for special treatment or for anyone to feel obligated to work with me. If they didn't want to help me, if there was a language barrier, or if they simply weren't interested, they could have just told me clearly. I would have accepted and respected that.

What disappoints me is the lack of communication and consideration after so many months, and especially after my mother came in person.

For me, honesty and empathy are fundamental, especially when someone explains that they are trying to rebuild their life and get ahead.

I simply expected a clear and sincere response.

"Update following owner's response" translates to:

Update following owner's response

Of course. Here is a faithful translation into Spanish, maintaining a firm but correct tone:

A correction:

I confirm that I sent a WhatsApp message in March 2026. The message was delivered correctly.

I repeat: I also sent a regular text message to your phone and received no reply.

Regarding the Instagram message, it appears as read. Contrary to your reply, it says "read" because my app is set to French. The read receipt is exactly the same on both my computer and my iPhone.

What you don't understand is that I fully understood you might be busy, and I would never say otherwise.

What bothers me is that this happened in March 2026, but what I find most difficult to understand is that the message appears as read, since the read receipt is the same for everyone.

If you had sent me a message, as you say, simply to tell me to be patient or that you had read my message, I could have waited two weeks or more if necessary.

And regarding my disability, yes, I contacted another center that was much more honest with me and is also used to working with people who have illnesses and disabilities like mine.

Therefore, the problem isn't the response time, because the same thing happens with another center here, and I completely understand that responses can take time. The problem is that you read the message and never replied.

You are human, and so am I.

I wish you all the best and continued success.

And this confirms that you are now responding very quickly after my negative review.

Goodbye.

one_star_reviews.text:
COMPLAINT OF PROFESSIONAL MALPRACTICE

After discovering that my child's mother had unilaterally contracted Anaïs's services to conduct psychological sessions with my son Michael, I immediately informed her that she had to cease any intervention. Likewise, I provided documentation proving that I share joint parental responsibility (pàtria potestat) and explained that joint authority includes decisions regarding his psychological care.

It was the professional's duty to verify parental responsibility and obtain proper consent before initiating therapy with a minor. However, once I contacted her directly and expressed my explicit opposition, Anaïs refused to acknowledge my position and maintained her intervention. She justified continuing treatment by relying on an erroneous interpretation of the following clause from our custody agreement:

'FIRST.- Parental authority, in application of the last paragraph of Article 156 of the Civil Code, shall be exercised by the mother, as she holds custody of the child.'
('PRIMERO.- La patria potestad en aplicación del artículo 156 CC último párrafo, será ejercida por la madre, por tener la custodia del mismo.')

Relying on this provision to justify unilateral mental healthcare represents a clear legal and deontological error:

1. Scope of Article 156 CC (Last Paragraph): This statutory provision applies strictly to routine, day-to-day care decisions (ejercicio ordinario de la custodia).
2. Extraordinary Decision: Under Spanish civil law and established jurisprudence, initiating psychological therapy with a minor is a non-routine, extraordinary decision (acto extraordinario de la patria potestad). It strictly requires the consent of both parents holding joint parental authority or prior judicial authorization.
3. Duty of Diligence: A daily custody reference does not grant unilateral authority over non-routine healthcare. Once I provided proof of joint parental responsibility and expressed explicit written opposition, professional diligence required halting treatment until mutual agreement was reached or judicial authorization was granted under Article 156 CC.

This matter is now formally before the Official College of Psychology of Catalonia (COPC), which has acknowledged receipt of my complaint to determine eventual professional and ethical responsibilities.

Anaïs, once I provided proof of my joint parental responsibility, it was no longer sufficient to rely on the account of one parent or on an incorrect legal interpretation. What is at stake here is the psychological intervention of a minor, my son Michael, and respect for the rights belonging to both parents. I will continue to defend my son's rights and my rights as a father through the appropriate formal channels so that no other minor or parent finds themselves in a similar situation.

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience with Beres Group.

After the end of our tenancy, a number of deductions were made from our deposit which we disputed, including €254.10 relating to a bathroom sink blockage, replacement costs for kitchen items, and an unusually expensive oven tray.

We raised detailed objections, provided our reasoning, and repeatedly tried to resolve the matter directly. Beres ultimately told us that it was acting only as an intermediary, that the deductions had been decided by the property owner, and that we should pursue the owner directly.

We therefore asked Beres to provide the owner’s legal name and contact details so that we could do exactly that. Despite giving them seven days to respond, we have received no reply.

Whatever the merits of an individual deposit dispute, I would expect a professional managing agent to deal with it transparently and to respond properly to reasonable correspondence. Instead, this has involved repeated chasing, inconsistent engagement and, ultimately, being directed to contact a landlord whose details Beres has then failed to provide.

A frustrating and unnecessarily difficult end to what should have been a straightforward tenancy.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am reporting the events of Saturday, September 19, 2026, at 7:00 PM, at the Lefties store in the Splau Shopping Center in Cornellà.

I went there with my partner and my young daughter. We used the self-checkout kiosks. I paid without checking, and as I was leaving, the security gate in the self-checkout area went off. An employee noticed that an item of clothing hadn't been scanned. I paid for it and left.

As I exited through the main door, the alarm went off again. A Prosegur security guard accused me, in front of my family, of stealing an item. I explained that it had already been checked three minutes earlier. To my surprise, when I went back inside, the sales assistant didn't remember checking the entire purchase.

I explained the error from a few minutes earlier and that they were having a software problem; the self-checkout machines weren't working properly. At that same moment, the same thing was happening to another customer with a young child. During the incident, the security gates kept going off for other customers.

I filled out the complaint form. The security guard was completely out of control. I asked for his name, and he refused to give it to me. He was shouting and behaving rudely in front of my daughter and other people with the same problem. The children ended up crying because of the tense situation. The store manager did nothing to control the situation.

I'm not filing a complaint... just a formal apology for the treatment I received and the ordeal my family went through. I work in customer service, and in my 30 years in the profession, I've never seen such a depressing situation.

Recommendations...

1. Review the self-checkout system.

2. Review Prosegur's protocol.

3. Provide staff training.

I reserve the right to submit this complaint form to the relevant authorities.

We almost returned a €200 purchase.

Lefties - Splau - Cornellà

As we were leaving with the twins' stroller, the alarm went off. We realized one of the little ones had hung up a child's umbrella. When we tried to return it, the Prosegur security guard told us we had to buy it. We explained it was a mistake, that we didn't want that umbrella, but he said that if we didn't pay for it, he would arrest us for shoplifting.

I was about to return a €200 purchase and buy the €5 umbrella instead. I think they should hire people with better eyesight to work at that entrance.

I'm not going back to that store.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am writing this review after an extremely unpleasant experience this morning at the Repsol gas station in Alcaraz. The lack of professionalism and the rudeness I received from the person in charge leave me no other option.
When I went to fill up with fuel (Efitec 95), the manager approached me in a completely inappropriate manner to reprimand me for not speaking to her before using the pump. She criticized me for putting in 98 instead of 95, arguing that it "was going to cost her money." I politely pointed out that the pumps are not properly identified or labeled to differentiate between the two fuels, so the confusion is a direct result of the lack of signage on her own pump, not customer negligence. The price difference between the two fuels was irrelevant to me; what is unacceptable is the dismissive treatment I received due to an organizational failure that is solely the responsibility of the station.

Later, when I went inside to pay, the employee apologized to me in a rather serious tone, which I accepted.
I told her that it's essential to be more tactful when dealing with the public and that the customer shouldn't have to bear the consequences of poor signage and management. However, as I was walking back to my car, the manager made comments again, this time in a lower voice, confirming a clear lack of respect for the customers. To avoid wasting more time, I didn't bother asking for a complaint form, but I certainly won't be refueling at this gas station again. A brand like Repsol shouldn't allow this lack of customer service or the absence of proper signage at its facilities.

one_star_reviews.text:
I've been going there and ordering delivery since they opened, as I live next door, and it's always been good. This past week, I went to the restaurant on a Thursday at 10:45 pm. The terrace was empty because it was hot, but I had my dog ​​with me, so I sat outside. They asked us, not very politely, to move tables because they were going to clear the terrace... 10:45 pm in the summer, I repeat... I replied that we had sat there because it was a bit cool, and she simply said, "I'm going to clear those tables."
When I ordered, I noticed they'd changed the menu, only the prices, by the way: garlic bread started at €4.95 and is now €7.95 (€8.95 with one topping). The children's menu is €2 more because the pizza is bigger, but they've removed the potatoes. I asked the waitress if the soft drink was a regular size or a large bottle like always, because in the latter case, I was sharing with my young son, and she said it was a regular size... No, it was a large bottle. He didn't even ask me what kind of crust I wanted, and I forgot to mention it. As soon as he left, I got up to confirm, and without answering, he went back into the kitchen. While we were eating, they quickly took over the entire terrace, leaving us alone. We ate, and at 11:25 pm, they started coming out one by one, three of them, to ask if we were okay, if we wanted anything, until I finally asked for the bill because I was feeling overwhelmed.
Anyway, one less pizzeria. I don't know if it's the change in staff or what, but what a disappointment.

I went there with the money and practically decided to buy a Kove 450, and I left without a bike and completely disillusioned.

The salesperson who helped me couldn't give me any basic information: no approximate arrival date, no maintenance intervals, and no realistic quote. He quoted me the list price for lowering the suspension when the final price is considerably cheaper. And regarding the power kit, which is an official Kove kit, they told me they don't install it (or the salesperson simply didn't know it existed).

To top it all off, they asked for a €1,000 deposit when, just days before, someone else from the same dealership had told me €500 on the phone.

I understand you can't know everything, but we're talking about an official dealership and a bike from their catalog. With that kind of service, it's impossible to build trust enough to hand over several thousand euros. I was going to buy it, and they completely killed my enthusiasm.

Avoid!! We rented a scooter through Rental Motor Bike, and besides the fact that the scooter fell apart and we almost stranded ourselves more than once, they returned our €300 deposit after more than a month, and ONLY after daily reminders and threats of legal action. So, I advise you not to give up and be a pain in the ass until the very end, otherwise, like so many others, you'll probably never get it back.

I rented a 50cc scooter from Jota Café Motocycle et Scooter in Ibiza during the summer. I want to share my experience factually, as several problems arose throughout the rental period.

Vehicle Pickup: No staff member was present at the agreed time for scooter delivery. I had to wait about an hour at the airport before receiving an answer by phone. When I picked up the vehicle, the only helmet provided in the top case was far too large; I had never been asked about it when booking or picking up the keys.

Customer Service Follow-up: Once my stay began, it proved impossible to contact the agency, either by phone or by going to the address listed on their website. Therefore, I was unable to get the ill-fitting helmet replaced and had to use it for the entire rental period.

Vehicle Condition: The scooter had several defects: it seemed to be modified and could exceed the legal speed limit for its engine size, the plastics were not holding up, the brakes were not working properly, the top case did not close properly in its housing, and traces of oil stained my clothes.

Terrible experience. The scooter was in deplorable condition, and the service was equally bad.

But the €300 deposit is just shameful. I waited the 10 business days they told me to, tried to contact them several times without response, and now, after more than 15 days, they want to keep part of my money because I returned it at 7:46 AM (I had notified them), even though they NEVER informed me of any penalty, not by text message, email, or when I returned it.

This is unacceptable, and I'm not going to let it go. I've already filed a complaint and I'm going to pursue this to the end to get my money back. Be very careful with this company because what they're doing is unacceptable. I absolutely do not recommend Jota Café Motor Bikes.

When I needed bodywork and paint repairs, I decided to take my car to Mercedes. I trusted the prestige of this car brand and, consequently, the bodywork specialists. I believed they would have a good repair method.

-What did I find after a while?
I took it in for two accidents on different dates.

-For the first accident, they only had the front bumper painted. I've attached a photo of what they did...

-For the second accident, they had the side painted, which will probably chip just like the front bumper. They left two clips broken from the roof trim and the door seal torn. They said the seal was broken before I even took it there. Luckily, I was able to prove it, and I saved myself €60, if not more, which is what the entire door seal costs.

-The second accident was for painting the side panel. On the other hand, when they painted the side, they got paint on both rims and tires because they didn't cover the area properly, and paint also got inside the car. I had to pay for a car wash to clean the entire interior! It took me a while to remove all the paint that got inside because they didn't properly close and seal the vehicle with tape and plastic before painting.

This is where you can see the difference in a job well done.

If you want to print, I recommend you find another print shop.

We'd been there for half an hour and I went inside to ask at the bar if we should order (thinking it was self-service since no one came to our table). It's a shame because the place is amazing, but the breakfast service leaves much to be desired. I imagine it's different for lunch or dinner, but I don't know. one_star_reviews.text:
The place is an old cider house remodeled in 2023 and given a facelift; the tables and chairs are very bulky and heavy. The service and friendliness were very good, but the food leaves a lot of room for improvement. The fabada (Asturian bean stew) served in those tiny red casseroles is clearly for people from outside Asturias. For an Asturian, those little casseroles, barely enough to fill a egret, feel meager, and the beans, hard as a rock and with very little flavor due to the lackluster accompaniments, are unexpected and disappointing. You can't cut corners on quality in dishes like this. The sea bream was nothing special, half a bream the size of an XS, and the pork knuckle was more bone than meat, served with bagged potato chips, just like the fish. It looks very bad on a Sunday menu to use pre-cooked products; they could save money there and not pay €10/kg for potatoes. They should invest in quality ingredients for a proper fabada.

The rice pudding was the only saving grace; it was very good and highly recommended.

The leftover plate from the appetizers, with its crumbs, remained with us throughout the meal. It wasn't removed, just like the rest of the service. This shows there's a lot of room for improvement in professionalism, aside from improving the service time between courses. Although, there's little that can be done if the only person serving is the cashier, taking orders, and tending the bar.
The holiday menu was €22, including coffee.

A very bad experience. We didn't even get to eat the dessert that came with the set menu.
The wait between courses was so long. The service was terrible; the waiter seemed to attend to tables randomly. Tables that arrived after us ate before us. The portions were very small and the food tasted very bland. A truly awful presentation.

one_star_reviews.text:
I want to leave this review to warn other users about something I consider very important.

My contract ended today, and, "as instructed," I called today to request cancellation.
To my surprise, they told me that, to make the cancellation effective, I had to receive a confirmation SMS that could take up to a week, and that in the meantime, I would have to continue paying.

Excuse me? If the contract ends today, why do I have to keep paying during the days it takes the company to process the cancellation internally?

If the confirmation SMS can take a week, there are simple solutions, such as marking the contract as "not to renew" on the end date and then processing the confirmation SMS. It doesn't seem reasonable to pass on to the customer the cost of an administrative or IT delay on the company's part.

And there's one detail I consider particularly significant: after complaining and expressing my complete dissatisfaction, the confirmation email arrived practically in a matter of seconds. So, how could they initially tell me the process could take a week?

I'm going to stay with the company because their prices are currently convenient for me, but that doesn't mean I'll accept any practice or stop warning other users.

Be very careful with contracts, especially with termination dates and cancellations. Keep all communications, emails, and any proof of your request.

If anyone finds themselves in the same situation and they try to charge them for days after the contract's termination date, I recommend filing a complaint and, if necessary, contacting consumer protection agencies or other relevant authorities.

Because it's one thing for a company to be late sending a text message, and quite another for them to try to charge the customer for that extra time when they've already requested cancellation on the agreed-upon date.

⭐️⭐️ Disappointing for a restaurant of this caliber and price.

We celebrated a birthday as a group, and despite having mentioned when booking that we would be bringing our own cake, no one informed us that we would be charged €10 PER PERSON simply for cutting and serving it. Given the size of our group, this amount is completely disproportionate and, above all, should have been communicated beforehand. When we expressed our disagreement, the only response we received was, "Sorry, we'll let you know next time." A clearly inadequate response to a charge we hadn't been informed about.

Furthermore, throughout the entire meal, we felt constant pressure to order, consume, and finish quickly. We understand that there are table reservations, but it's very uncomfortable to celebrate a special occasion constantly checking the time and feeling that the staff is in a hurry for you to leave. When the time came, we were asked to leave the table and go to the bar, making it virtually impossible to enjoy a relaxed after-dinner conversation with the whole group.

What should have been a special experience ended up giving us the feeling that table turnover and consumption take precedence over hospitality and customer enjoyment. This is especially unpleasant when you're celebrating a birthday and have chosen an establishment of this caliber for the occasion.

Clearly, we won't be returning, nor can we recommend it to our friends and acquaintances. Furthermore, given the lack of a satisfactory solution, we will consider formally filing a complaint through the appropriate channels (official complaint form and Catalan Consumer Agency), particularly regarding the charge for a service whose price was not disclosed to us beforehand.

It's a shame, because we expected so much more from COYA Barcelona.

Extremely unpleasant atmosphere due to the rude and impolite service from the staff.

We were practically kicked out of our table by a man with long hair.

He kept implying that we weren't going to eat anything, that we were just drinking beer, and this was less than 30 minutes after we arrived.

Terrible.

It's a shame we couldn't try it because of the bad attitude of the long-haired waiter with earrings... He only let us sit down if we ate at least 5 pintxos per person... So we decided to give our hunger and money to the bar across the street and we loved it! King Pincho: delicious pintxos, great variety, good price, and the waiters were the friendliest!

We wanted to have a few beers and some tapas, but a waiter gave us a really bad experience. He was short, dark-haired, with a bit of a belly. We went across the street and had a fantastic dinner, great drinks, and the best price. Don't go there, go across the street to King Pinchos.

We were served by a very unfriendly person with long hair who told us that if we didn't have dinner, we'd have to leave. We really wanted to have a refreshing drink and then decide whether to eat or not, but he didn't give us a chance and kicked us out. We couldn't choose or enjoy the place, and we really had to leave. We went to King Pinchos next door, and they treated us like royalty. The waiters were very friendly, and the skewers were top quality.

I went on Saturday evening, it had been a while since I'd been, and I wanted to go with two friends who were visiting from outside Barcelona. Back in the day (about three years ago), it was really good; the waiters were different, not the same ones as here. We sat inside because he said it was nice, the air conditioning was on... but it was so low they even had the windows open. So, to be a bit more comfortable, we saw a table outside and said we'd move. To our surprise, they didn't like it. We explained why, but it was all the same to him. The only thing he could think of was to tell us that if we wanted to sit outside, we'd each have to order four pintxos. I told him I was from here and that's not how things work. To avoid upsetting my friends, I decided to let it go and leave, but that doesn't mean I won't explain the situation. And he should know that next time I will call the police and have them explain it to them.

A place with absolutely no sense of order, and they don't respect the customer.
Every day is a different experience.
One day you might have a good experience and everything goes well; the food is very good, the young woman is friendly, and the older lady is in charge.

We weren't even lucky enough for her to say hello or come over to talk to us; she was talking loudly as she paced around the place like she was herding cattle.

I won't be going back.

The first day, my partner and I arrived for dinner at 10:15 pm and were told the kitchen was already closed, even though they officially close at 11:30 pm.

The next day, we had lunch and told the woman who had served us very kindly that we would return that evening to try the pizzas. We went early, around 9:10 pm, and when we arrived, the woman looked at us and waved her hand dismissively, but the girl behind the counter gave us the go-ahead to sit at an empty table. The woman quickly approached us and told us, in the most rude manner and without the same friendliness as at lunchtime, that we couldn't sit down because they were already closed due to a high volume of orders. It left us feeling awful. It was early, and we had no problem waiting if there was a delay; we just wanted to try the pizzas and have a good time. We sat on a bench on the other corner looking for somewhere else to eat, while we watched a group of six young people approach. They were seated and served. They hadn't told us they worked with reservations, so 2 + 2 = 4, and math doesn't lie: 6 is more than 2. That's what matters.

Customer service is often relegated to the bottom of the list of priorities. A serious mistake. And even worse when arrogance, a lack of empathy, and poor treatment take over, obscuring the simplest fact: when a customer is on vacation or simply wants to eat out, they spend their hard-earned money, money they could use for something else, to pay for a dinner like this one. The last thing they want to feel is that their choice is modest, superfluous, or worthless, compared to all the other options available. A disservice.

Today they lost a customer. Tomorrow could bring lean times. I hope I don't find them resting in the comfort of mediocrity.

one_star_reviews.text:
Excellent care, incompetent doctor.

I must say that all the professionals who have treated us each time we've gone have been outstanding, from the emergency room receptionists to the nurses and pediatricians.

However, the excellent work of these professionals is overshadowed by a mediocre doctor who has seen us several times. My wife is breastfeeding our one-year-old baby. Every time this doctor (a relatively young man) sees us, he gives us a lecture about how the child is too old to breastfeed, and even though we specifically ask him not to, he always prescribes things incompatible with breastfeeding. And it's not out of necessity, since we've been treated for the same thing at other hospitals without having the same problem. This last time, he didn't even ask us; he simply injected my wife with whatever he thought was necessary and told us about it afterward, while telling us ONCE AGAIN that the child is too old and that this is an excellent opportunity to wean him. When all the professionals who have seen our child have told us that ideally he should be breastfed (in addition to solid foods) until he is two years old. Normally I wouldn't complain, but I've grown tired of seeing my son spend sleepless nights because of that person who is hardly a doctor. We sincerely hope we never cross paths with that man again. Otherwise, we will have to stop going to this hospital, where the other professionals treat us so well.

I am a regular customer of Casa Carmen in Barcelona, ​​where I frequently go with my husband, who is from Barcelona. I know the restaurant and its menu very well. I want to make something VERY clear: I AM NOT A PROSTITUTE. I am a working woman, an architect, and a lawyer, and I will not accept anyone making assumptions about me, my profession, or my character simply because of my nationality, my appearance, or the fact that I was alone.

I ordered a salad and an orange juice because I know the menu perfectly and knew exactly what I wanted to eat. I didn't need anyone to tell me what to order or make me feel like I wasn't a suitable person to be in the restaurant.

I felt truly humiliated and left without ordering a single thing.

This isn't going to end here. I'm already reporting the incident to management and my lawyer, and I'm going to explore the appropriate legal options.

It's especially disappointing because I went there precisely because I know and like Casa Carmen in Barcelona. I never expected to receive this kind of treatment at a restaurant in the same chain.

What happened to me is unacceptable, and I'm not going to let it go.

My experience with Fitness Park has been very disappointing, especially regarding the handling of my cancellation request.

I requested to cancel my membership and communicated with the gym, explaining my situation. At that time, the outstanding balance was approximately €27. Later, after changing my job and moving to Huelva, I inquired about my membership and continued as a client.

Some time later, I was informed that my cancellation had not been processed and that, since I had stopped paying, the fees had continued to accrue, reaching a debt of over €100.

What I find particularly concerning is that, according to the information I received during the process, I was not clearly informed that the cancellation was not being processed and that the fees would continue to accrue. I have requested a review of my file, the communications, and the breakdown of the amount owed, but so far, I have not received a satisfactory solution.

For this reason, I have decided to file a formal complaint so that the case can be reviewed.

Terrible Management and Violation of Rights
I am leaving this review to publicly denounce the arbitrary, unilateral, and completely disproportionate treatment I received at this center from the manager.
I went to formally report an extremely serious situation: a gym employee was taking pictures of me with his personal cell phone inside the facilities, completely violating my right to privacy and data protection. The manager's response was outrageous: he claimed to have no explanation, refused to listen to me, and closed the matter completely arbitrarily, ignoring my version of events.

To make matters worse, I have been expelled from the center alleging supposed prior "verbal warnings." I categorically deny these accusations: there is no evidence of such warnings, I received no notification on the club's app, no calls, and no warning emails. A unilateral decision was made without giving me the opportunity to defend myself or justify anything.

I demand a formal, written response from Fitness Park management regarding this injustice and the manager's inaction in the face of his staff's inappropriate conduct. I do not recommend this gym to anyone seeking a safe environment and professional service.

I'm here to tell you about the experience six of us had yesterday for dinner.

It's the first time in my life I've had to get up from a table and leave without dinner after waiting an hour and a half.

We had a reservation for six people at 10:00 PM, we sat down quickly, and by 10:15 PM we had already ordered. Our first surprise was that the waitress who served us didn't write down anything (right in front of us) about what we had ordered.

Around 10:50 PM they brought us some complimentary tortilla chips to snack on, and at 11:10 PM the nachos we had ordered arrived.

People were starting to get a little listless and, frankly, didn't feel like eating much, but we decided to wait a little longer. Around 11:25 pm, they came to offer us a complimentary beer, but no one at the table was thirsty; we were just hungry and quite annoyed.

At 11:30 pm, we got up from the table because we couldn't wait any longer and were starving. We went to pay, but they told us it wasn't necessary, that they would cover it. A nice gesture. What surprised me most was that, after waiting an hour and a half, our food wasn't about to arrive (we had ordered tacos).

Above all, what bothered us most, besides waiting an hour and a half without being able to eat, was how they handled the situation. When the nachos arrived, all they could think to say was, "Good things come to those who wait," which only made the table more irritated than anything else.

We also commented that if they had warned us before we sat down that the place was packed, we might have considered whether or not to sit down. We felt like they hadn't taken our order and were just waiting for us to leave, because waiting an hour and a half for tacos is NOT NORMAL.

Anyway, we came looking forward to having some tacos for dinner and they completely ruined the experience. I wouldn't recommend this place to anyone. The worst part is that we really liked this place (we'd been to their Raval location before) and because of this experience, we won't be going back.

one_star_reviews.text:
Terrible
⭐ 1/5

A complete lack of professionalism and foresight.

The school year has just begun, and we're already finding that there are no classes this week because the center doesn't have the computers, networks, and resources ready to teach normally. After four or five months of vacation, it's hard to understand why there wasn't enough time to have the facilities and equipment ready before the start of the school year.

However, they were quick to collect the fees, and rather high ones at that: they were already collecting them on September 2nd.

And the worst part is that this isn't a one-off or an exception: it's been going on for several years, and the same thing happens at the beginning of every school year. One year there are no teachers, another year there's construction, another year the computers or networks aren't ready… There's always some problem that prevents classes from starting normally.

And throughout the year, the situation continues: when it's not one thing, it's another. Whether it's a teacher shortage, malfunctioning equipment, network outages, or a lack of necessary resources… there's always some problem that ends up disrupting the normal flow of classes.

This isn't just a one-off lapse in foresight, but a systematic lack of organization and planning.

The impression the school gives is that collecting fees is the priority, while the organization and provision of educational services are relegated to a secondary concern.

I believe that both the Ministry of Education and the Community of Madrid should seriously review the operation of this school and the conditions under which it receives and manages public grants and subsidies. When a family pays significant sums for an education, the bare minimum is that the teachers, classrooms, and resources needed to deliver the classes are available.

After witnessing this exact same situation repeated time and again, it's difficult not to consider it a lack of professionalism and respect for the students and their families.

If you're thinking of enrolling at this school, don't. It's a waste of money.

My parents had already made a €300 reservation and were explaining everything to us, but yesterday they called to say there weren't enough students and it wouldn't be possible. This comes after other centers had already rejected my application. One of their employees continued talking to my parents, telling them everything they needed to do regarding the payment process, and then yesterday I found out there weren't enough students. They could have said that before we paid; it seems they're only interested in your money.
It is incomprehensible and inconceivable that a concert and performance hall should have such terrible sound. It's bad for both the artists and their audience.

one_star_reviews.text:
Our building manager sought proposals from several lawyers, and we chose this firm because they specialized exclusively in construction damage claims, had good reviews, and mentioned having dealt with this construction company before with positive results.

The expert they assigned prepared a comprehensive and detailed report of all the reported damages, which ultimately amounted to €268,000.

During the two years the process lasted, we didn't receive a single visit from this lawyer, nor did he show any interest in meeting with the residents or the president, stating that the report was all he needed. He also never visited the building.

One month before the trial, the construction company made a verbal settlement offer of €70,000, which the lawyer presented to us as a possible way to avoid the trial, or as an opportunity for us to submit a counteroffer. Since the outstanding damages largely consisted of leaks and dampness, which weren't covered, we decided to go to court, confident in our choice of a lawyer specializing in construction damages (the most expensive of all the options the building manager gave us).

When the trial arrived, the lawyer didn't provide us with any feedback. Two months later, the verdict was a bitter pill to swallow: the judge almost entirely sided with the construction company's expert report, awarding us €15,000 in compensation out of the €268,000 our community had claimed. Seeing that figure, we wondered what could have happened, since we had researched that compensation usually ranges from 20% to 80% of the amount claimed, and in our case, it was barely 5%.

The lawyer stated that he didn't know what could have happened because, in his opinion, the process had proceeded normally. One of our neighbors, who is also a lawyer, requested the construction company's expert report and the video recording of the trial. Upon reviewing the recording, we found that our expert witness's work was quite weak: on several occasions, he was asked questions he couldn't answer, responding verbatim, "I don't remember, but you can check it in the report."

The opposing side gave a 45-minute presentation in which, using a tablet, they dismantled our report point by point. When the construction company's expert witness finished testifying and it was our lawyer's turn to ask questions, he simply asked, "Have you visited the community?" to which the expert witness replied yes, and the lawyer indicated he had no further questions.

We were utterly astonished to find that he didn't raise any additional questions or a single objection. The most striking case: our bill for leaks and dampness amounted to €108,000, and the construction company proposed resolving it for €175 (a solution that doesn't even eliminate the leaks they themselves acknowledge, but rather diverts them through a drainage channel). Our lawyer offered no arguments, asked no questions, and didn't defend the report we had paid for. He left us completely unprotected.

When we later called him to ask if he was available for a residents' meeting at 7 pm, he told us he was off duty. In that same conversation, our neighbor, who is also a lawyer, asked him why he hadn't refuted the other lawyer's arguments or asked any questions. His response, with utter arrogance, was that this had been his strategy, and that he considered he had done a great job.

I absolutely do not recommend this firm. Their negligence and inaction, their complete lack of interest in preparing for the trial, have resulted in the construction company getting off scot-free, and each resident will have to contribute €8,000 to cover the damages we believe were poorly represented in court, in addition to fees that represent 50% of the compensation obtained.

*REVIEW EDIT*: All the effort they lack in defending their clients, they more than make up for in posting their own reviews to inflate the rating, all of them right after our community's review on June 26th.

Good afternoon,
This is a truly terrible repair shop, and the customer service from the person who receives the cars is absolutely appalling.

Getting any information from the shop is impossible, no matter how many messages you leave on the answering machine or with the secretaries who claim they'll pass them on.
I have comprehensive car insurance with a mutual insurance company, and when I filed the claim, they told me there was no problem and that the car would be ready in approximately 15 days. Since it wasn't ready by that date, they gave me a story about how my insurance company hadn't authorized everything from the beginning and they had to request an extension 15 days after I filed the claim.
I spoke with the insurance company, and they assured me that everything was authorized from the start. However, the shop didn't even start repairing the car until 15 days later.

The car was in the shop for 28 days.

Therefore, I don't recommend this shop to anyone, and I encourage everyone who has had such a bad experience to do the same. P.S. Don't go to this workshop/dealership

Watch out!! What a rip-off the service was! Definitely the last time I'll go. Plus, they gave me back the car dirty on the outside. I didn't like it at all. I took it to my usual garage because it was closed for vacation, and what a mistake! They're just ripping you off. I used to go to the Alcorcón garage, but they've moved the whole Nissan dealership to Leganés. I wouldn't recommend that garage at all.

It's a shame I can't give less than one star.
It took a month to deliver the car, and I received absolutely no information during that time, even after calling someone named "Carlos" weekly. I dropped off the car on August 19th with an appointment and requested a courtesy car, which was never provided. Carlos was never available. I asked that if the insurance adjuster didn't accept something, they should indicate it, as it was a collision, so we could file another claim with our insurance company and have the car fully repaired. The car was delivered today with one bumper still unrepaired.
It's best to find another dealership. You can skip the "let's write to you to discuss your problem" bit, as it's pointless. However, I will be filing a formal complaint with the appropriate authorities and another through my insurance company to prevent other customers from taking their cars to this dealership. Not a single communication from the dealership in a month, and I called three times a week without getting any response. The remaining repairs will be taken to a proper garage.

I'm not at all happy with the work done at the garage: they installed the windshield incorrectly, another time the hood was dislodged, another time the paint had orange peel texture and they didn't even fill a scratch. I'm not going back, I'm sorry, but every time I take the car in I find that the work hasn't been done properly.

I've been trying to get an appointment for three weeks, and they finally gave me one for today, Monday, September 14th, at 7:15 AM. They told me they don't have the part. I have a 2025 Interstar van, and for the past month, I've been hearing the brake pads squealing. They gave me an appointment, and when I went to the dealership, they told me they didn't have the part and that even the factory doesn't have it because it's a very new model.

So my question is, why are they selling a van if they don't have the part and it's not even manufactured yet? On top of that, they quoted me an exorbitant price of €790 for the front and rear brake pads! So I have to keep working like this, and God forbid my brake disc gets damaged? Now I have to wait a week or even a month for a part. It's unbelievable!

Horrible experience with the garage. I took my car in at 9 a.m. for its annual service. After 5 hours, when I went to pick it up, they still hadn't even touched it. The excuse was that the garage was overwhelmed, which, considering what they charge for labor and the number of people you can see inside, seems insane.
On the one hand, the key collector and salesperson, Carlos, had a terrible attitude towards me, even making defensive comments and accusing me of speaking rudely to him, when nothing of the sort had happened. He seemed offended that I wanted to take my car before the garage had even been opened.
On the other hand, the reception staff did everything they could to help me. These contrasting actions reflect well on both the garage and the staff.

My experience has been very disappointing. I went in for cosmetic restorations on four teeth and made it very clear that I wanted a natural result and for the color to match my teeth. I even asked to have just one done first to check the outcome.

In the end, they did all four. Two turned out acceptable, but two didn't, and one ended up with a clearly darker area that is very noticeable, especially in photos. I have before-treatment photos that clearly show my tooth didn't look like that.

When I complained about the result, I simply wanted them to review and fix the tooth that had turned out badly. However, instead of focusing on that problem, they scheduled me for other treatments on another molar. This was incomprehensible to me and increased my concern even more.

They also suggested restoring the entire tooth to achieve a uniform color. I believe that if a treatment doesn't turn out as requested, the first step should be to listen to the patient and find a solution to the problem, not steer the conversation toward other treatments.

But what disappointed me most was the lack of transparency regarding the costs. They even tried to charge me €90 for an X-ray that I had already had done through my insurance and given to the clinic. Finally, after explaining the situation, they told me I didn't have to pay for it. As I left, still in the X-ray, they told me I had to pay €50 for a treatment check-up. I was in shock right there... I was leaving with teeth I wasn't happy with because I couldn't even smile, and they were already thinking about what else they could extract...

After everything that happened, I have completely lost faith in this clinic. I wouldn't go back and I would never recommend it.

one_star_reviews.text:
Yesterday, my family and I ate at this restaurant for the second time, and frankly, the experience left much to be desired.

As soon as we arrived, they asked if we wanted to sit inside or outside. We chose outside, and the waiter immediately warned us that wasps might get into our food. I completely understand that this can happen on a terrace, but the way he said it and the overall welcome didn't make us feel particularly comfortable.

During the meal, the service was quite slow. There were long waits between courses, even though it wasn't very busy at the time. Several times I tried to call the waiter over to order a drink, and he wouldn't even look at me; he just walked right past us and, after a long while, finally appeared at our table.

But there's something I'd like to highlight in particular: these days, considering the number of people with food allergies and intolerances, I find it quite disappointing that they don't offer lactose-free milk. What surprised us most was that they told us they had semi-skimmed milk, as if that were an alternative. One thing has nothing to do with the other. If someone is lactose intolerant, whether the milk is semi-skimmed or whole makes absolutely no difference, because both can contain lactose.

It's a shame, because as it was our second visit, we expected a much better experience. The food might be okay, but customer service, attention, and consideration for dietary needs are also part of the experience. And this time, frankly, we left quite disappointed.

one_star_reviews.text:
Hahaha, they've blocked me on Facebook and Instagram, what a bunch of jerks! 😂😂😂 That's why you don't see any reviews from dissatisfied customers.

I'll try to summarize the disaster that was the bathroom renovation with Renoveduch.

I'll start by saying that after this renovation with Renoveduch, another bathroom was done in this house, and two more at a relative's house.

*NONE OF THEM WITH RENOVEDUCH*

The only thing they were punctual about was the start and completion dates.

When they left, everything seemed fine, but the next day the surprises began: a considerable hole in the wall, hidden behind a piece of bedroom furniture. The bathroom door wouldn't close properly; it was misaligned. But what really infuriated us was seeing two significant dents in the shower tray, one below the faucets and the other on the exposed edge. This outraged us, as the installers must have clearly seen it when they installed it and grouted the floor.

We contacted Renoveduch, and the repair technician started coming to our house.

After this, the grout where the floor met the shower tray began to peel.
Another call to Renoveduch and another visit from the technician.
Later, the grout where the shower tray met the walls started to come loose. This wasn't just an aesthetic problem, as it could cause leaks to the floor below. Another visit from the technician.

Several weeks after the work was completed, the sales representative contacted us to check on our satisfaction. We explained all the problems we were having, and he said he would call us back later with an explanation. That was at the beginning of 2022, and I'm still waiting for that call.

Continuing with the problems, the toilet bowl started moving excessively.
The technician came back to my house and applied two tubes of silicone sealant between the water tank and the wall, without any screws to the floor, because, as he told me, since the drain runs across the wall, one of the screws could puncture the drain. I told him that the appropriate screw could be used on the side where the drain wasn't causing the problem, and a shorter screw on the side where it was, since there would be some support between the tile and the sealant. In short, the toilet is only held to the wall with silicone. When I have to replace any mechanism and disassemble the cistern, I'm going to remember RENOVEDUCH'S Bungling Services.

The grout lifted in a new spot.

Technician visit.

Well, after all this, it seems we're finally getting rid of the problems, but no!!

The toilet was splashing water outside. At first, we thought it was just a bad flush by some guy using the bathroom.

Until we realized that when we flushed, it splashed quite a bit. We called Renoveduch, the technician came, adjusted the flush flow, and it seemed to solve the problem, but by changing the flow, it wasn't flushing all the waste. A few weeks later, they replaced the toilet, and after scrutinizing the issue, we saw that it was still doing the exact same thing. A few weeks later, they replaced the toilet again, this time with a similar model, but not the same as the one we chose. Well, it seems that problem is finally solved.

Edit 12-2023.
It seems the tile was cut with chunks or pliers; the silicone is starting to give way, and new damage is appearing. How long will we keep discovering hidden problems?

Now they no longer cover hidden defects; the two-year warranty has expired. They'd come to my house for the modest price of €100.

What luck we had with these crooks!

And now, after two and a half years and several eye surgeries, I'm regaining some vision and I can see the broken eyelids that were placed. I'm attaching a photo to prove it.

Now that you've read this and many other negative reviews about their shoddy work, it's up to you. Unfortunately, I wasn't informed.

one_star_reviews.text:
A review to draw some conclusions.
I went there following Google Maps directions. Terrible experience. I went in, said good morning as my parents taught me. The waiter's manners were minimal, if not nonexistent; he didn't even bother to say hello! I waited to be served, and there were few customers in the place. Except for one who ordered a coffee, everyone else was being served, even though there were two other waitresses. (One of them was in the storeroom and the other was looking at her phone with a customer.) Zero empathy. I ordered a coffee and a hot chocolate, and he served them to me on the bar, which I couldn't reach because there was a customer in front of me and he couldn't bring it closer. I had to stand on my tiptoes and stretch my whole arm out to get it, and I'm 178 cm tall.
It felt like indifference, apathy, or even mocking the customer who pays the bills. If he were my employee, he'd either change his attitude or he'd be out on the street for sure. I didn't say anything to avoid making a scene, but I really should have asked for the complaint form. Customers should be treated politely, and I don't hesitate to tell them to let me know if they have any problems. (My boss, very wise by the way, used to say that a customer is hard to win and easy to lose.) Anyway! Riaño and its surroundings are beautiful places that had a lot of problems with the construction of a reservoir, and people like this don't do the town or tourism any favors. The people of León don't have that kind of attitude, and I'm very grateful for the behavior of the people in the area during the eight days I spent there, from León city to the last village in El Bierzo. I'm very happy going to that wonderful region, and it really bothers me that there are people who think anything goes when it comes to tourism.

P.S. Since he threatened me for posting a photo where a customer's face was visible, I apologize for that and deleted the review and the photo, but now I'm posting it without harming the customers who are innocent. There are photos of customers in the restaurant and on the terrace where you can see their faces, so I imagine from the reviews that it must be something personal, and everyone who tells the truth is wrong except him. Best regards, and I hope he gets the same treatment you give others, whether you're a waiter or the owner, because it makes no difference to me. Long live León!

Quiet, easy to talk

My experience at Hello Nails Travessera de Dalt was unfortunately very disappointing. On August 7th, I went to have my semi-permanent manicure removed (€13.90). The initial service was very good, and in fact, I left with a positive impression of the salon. I mentioned that I had a wedding coming up and wanted a specific design, and both the employee and the manager were very attentive and encouraged me to book a manicure and pedicure as well. Before booking, I clearly explained that on August 13th, I had to leave the salon by 2:00 PM at the latest due to work commitments. I even offered to do my manicure and pedicure on different days if they weren't sure they could finish on time. They assured me there wouldn't be a problem and gave me an appointment for 11:30 AM. On the day of the appointment, I arrived before the agreed time, but the service started late, and the pedicure finished at approximately 12:30 PM. Seeing that there wasn't enough time to do my nails properly before 2:00 PM, I suggested rescheduling the manicure for another day. The salon agreed. However, as I was leaving, the manager made me return and told me I would have to pay a supposed "penalty" for the time they had reserved for me, stating it was a "Headquarters" policy. When I asked how much this supposed penalty was, I wasn't even given a specific amount. This happened in front of other employees and another client, making me feel extremely uncomfortable. Furthermore, they had previously asked me for a €35 deposit via Bizum, supposedly also on Headquarters' instructions. When I later requested a refund because I no longer wanted to continue with the service at that salon, I was told there were no refunds. Given all of this, I contacted Hello Nails Customer Service, and here's one of the most worrying parts: the main office confirmed by phone that the information I had received from the salon regarding the penalty, the deposit, and the refund policy was incorrect. They apologized for what happened and asked me to submit a written complaint. Later, the salon itself contacted me again directly via WhatsApp from a different number to contradict my complaint and maintain their version of events. The situation was even more uncomfortable, especially after I had already formally reported the matter to the main office. There are also inconsistencies in the breakdown of expenses that the establishment later provided. The amounts they listed don't match the outstanding amount they claim I owed, so I'm still waiting for a clear explanation and a correct breakdown. As for the service, the pedicure decorations started coming off approximately one week later. I won't go into all the conversations I had with the salon here, but I have the messages and payment receipts, and I've provided them to Hello Nails main office. The most disappointing thing isn't just the money, but the lack of transparency, the contradictory information, and the way they handled a situation that could have been resolved simply by acknowledging that the schedule didn't allow for both services to be performed comfortably. Precisely because my first visit had been good, I decided to give them another chance for a more elaborate service. After this experience, I won't be returning to this establishment, and frankly, I'll think long and hard before using another center of this brand. I hope that Head Office thoroughly investigates what happened and takes the necessary steps to prevent other customers from finding themselves in a similar situation.

one_star_reviews.text: I've been coming to this place for over three years and I've never been as disappointed as I was today. To begin with, even though they weren't busy, it took them about half an hour to bring a single ramen (the rest obviously took even longer). The tofu salad arrived with raw tofu, and the guy had the nerve to tell me that's always been the case, as if we'd never ordered it. Then a Roujiamo arrived with raw bread, which we sent back, and another raw one arrived. And they tell me we can't return it, even though we didn't eat it because we couldn't eat the raw bread. When the girl in charge or the manager is there, everything is fine, but when she's not, it's a complete disaster. What a shame they have such a bad staff.

My partner and I came to eat here. It's not our first time, and we keep coming back because we really like it. But today's experience left us speechless. The roujiamo was raw inside (smelling of raw flour), and the tofu salad was raw. The ramen and the braised beef were good, cooked perfectly and delicious, but the most disappointing thing was the staff's response.
We approached them respectfully to explain that both the tofu salad and the roujiamo were raw, and their response was that "it's always been like this," even though it's not the first time we've eaten here. We sent both dishes back, and they asked if we wanted to exchange them. We said no to the salad, but yes to the roujiamo, and when it came back, it was raw again; we didn't even get a bite. The response was that "it can't be returned and it can't be removed from the bill." All of this was said by the waiter because neither the chef nor the manager dared to come out and offer an explanation. We won't be back. We are very disappointed with this site.

one_star_reviews.text: And I can't give it less because I can't. Eight nurses smoking outside, four chatting in one of the examination rooms, and my partner waiting seven hours for someone to see her. It's a disgraceful place. On top of that, I can't accompany her because supposedly companions aren't allowed inside unless absolutely necessary, but everyone inside has a companion and we, a young couple, can't. I find it appalling. It's a disgraceful place and a disgrace to the staff who only come here to kill time and pocket their paycheck.
Nobody answers the phone, it's awful.

Today I had to go to the emergency room. My experience was awful. I had to go because I have a herniated disc at L4-L5 pinching my sciatic nerve. I was waiting to be called for surgery. I couldn't walk. When I entered the emergency room, they gave me a wheelchair, and while I was waiting to be called, I heard two orderlies arguing about the wheelchairs, saying they were theirs. A little while later, they approached me, and one of them said, "This one's yours." They made me change chairs, and I changed without saying anything. I find it shameful that they argue over something like that, as if it were a school playground. Finally, they called me. I told the orthopedist what was wrong, and he said they were going to give me some medication through an IV. They took me to the treatment room. The nurses were laughing and chatting about their lives as if they didn't have jobs. I asked for a sheet because it was too cold, but they ignored me. After a long while, I asked again, and they said, "I'll go get it." After a long time, I tried to get up because they weren't paying attention to me. The gentleman who was with the other nurse... The woman next to me saw me and offered to go and ask for it. Finally, they brought it over. All this time, they haven't given me any medication to take away the pain, and of course, the doctor hasn't shown up. He's been behind every curtain except mine. I overheard them talking. "This is the girl behind the last curtain. We'd forgotten she was there." Next time I go to the ER, I'm wearing a neon sign so they don't forget me. I kept quiet so as not to cause a scene. This isn't the way to treat patients. Anyway, I had to leave the ER with the same pain I came in with, listening to nonsense from the nurses and orderlies.

I agree with the reviews and comments: going to the emergency room (which we all enjoy, of course) and then being charged for parking as if you were out partying is enough to make you angry, to say the least. But I think all we can do is complain; it's something, at least.

Every time I've had to go, the treatment of the patient and family members has been deplorable. Some orderlies think they're sheriffs, they're not friendly at all, they treat you like you're stupid and think they're above good and evil, they make you feel like you're bothering them.

one_star_reviews.text: Last night, three friends and I went out for dinner. It took them over half an hour to serve us and another half hour to bring out any food. And when they finally brought a dish, oh my god! It was awful! Each course was slower and worse than the last. I said, "Please, bring me something else to eat, because we didn't like anything we ordered." And they said, "The kitchen's closed!" 😂😂😂😂😂 Not even a piece of cheese! We were starving! They brought us coffee and shots and then immediately kicked us out, saying they were closing. Goodbye! We'll never go back! What a terrible experience!

My goodness! I've never experienced anything like this in Spain! After an hour and 50 minutes, they told us we needed to leave the table because they had other customers, and the reservation system didn't mention anything about us only having two hours, nothing at all! And we had wine in our glasses, which they brought just a minute before telling us we needed to leave. Unbelievable and unprecedented!

A truly disappointing experience and, above all, absolutely unacceptable customer service.

From the beginning, we felt rushed, without understanding why. And finally, about ten minutes before our two-hour reservation was up, they literally came to ask us to leave, while we still had food and drinks on the table.

We explained that we still had wine in our glasses and that, obviously, we couldn't just get up and leave. The response was, basically, that they then had to tell customers they had to leave.

The problem is that at no point were we informed that the reservation was limited to two hours. In fact, we've checked the website where we made the reservation again, and there's absolutely no indication of this time limit. If such a condition exists, the least they can do is inform the customer before they sit down, not come and ask them to leave while they're still eating or drinking.
The worst part isn't even the two-hour limit. It's the way they handled it. They made us feel like we had to leave, as if we'd done something wrong, when we were simply enjoying our food and drinks.
A restaurant can have its rules and arrange its tables however it wants. But if a rule directly affects the customer experience, it must be communicated clearly and in advance. And certainly, literally kicking customers out with their drinks still on the table is not an acceptable way to treat anyone. They completely ruined our experience, and we left with a very unpleasant feeling. The food might be okay… but the service and customer care are a fundamental part of the experience. And in our case, it was a 1/5.
